title: Ester + 2 RMgX → 3° alcohol (adds twice)
reagentDisplay: 1. CH3MgBr (2 equiv or excess), ether  2. H3O+
why: The first methyl adds and methoxide leaves (add, then eliminate), giving a ketone. That ketone is more reactive than the starting ester, so a second equivalent adds right away. Two identical R groups end up on the old carbonyl carbon.

traps.explains: The ketone does form, but it's more reactive than the ester and the Grignard is still there, so it doesn't stop. To stop at a ketone, use R2CuLi with an acid chloride.
This tetrahedral intermediate doesn't survive. An ester carbon has a leaving group (methoxide), so it collapses back to C=O.
This has only one new methyl and an extra H. Grignards deliver carbon, not hydride, and they add twice to esters.

review: Key step shown is the first addition (Grignard + ester). Check this is the step students should be drilled on.
